_: The observation contract from spec/MEDIA.md as data: `contract` is what every medium must answer; each medium's `row` is the worked example (drafts for the agent to sharpen against the repo); `residue` is what only a human can answer, phrased for that medium. A test keeps this in lockstep with MEDIA.md.

contract.question: Where does the behavior manifest to whoever consumes it?
What is the concrete observable you assert, never mere presence?
What operation commits the effect, at the end of the flow?
What does 'the build that carries your commit' mean here?
Where is the same pattern re-implemented?
What automated test or re-runnable command re-proves it, red-before / green-after?
Where do producer and consumer update independently?

reach.question: How does an agent reach the place where the behavior is observable, and what access does that need?
Any shortcut that makes it reachable or reproducible without production access?
Does the verify environment hold realistic data or inputs, or must something be seeded first?
Any behavior not observable through the primary tool named in observe-by? (comma-separated)

row.value: DOM text / input.value / aria state / rendered row count; for a 'not showing' symptom the RENDERED output, never the API/DB that feeds it, and count parity for a rendered collection

residue.access: How does an agent reach a signed-in state on the verify environment? (test account / dev bypass / none needed)
residue.shortcut: Any dev-mode shortcut that makes it reachable? (fixed OTP, seeded login, magic link, flag)
residue.fixtures: Does that environment carry realistic data, or must a surface be seeded first?
residue.special_surfaces: Any surfaces that must be driven in a BROWSER rather than by API? (rendered PDFs, print views)

row.build_artifact: the deployed service (sha via /health or the deployments API)
row.receipt: a request/integration test, or receipt-cmd: one curl asserting status/body (-f fails on non-2xx, expect:/.../ on the body; one command, no pipes)

residue.access: How does an agent authenticate to the verify environment's API? (bearer or service token, test client credentials, none needed)
residue.shortcut: Any dev-mode shortcut? (static token, auth-off flag, seeded API client)
residue.fixtures: Does the environment hold realistic records, or must rows be seeded before an endpoint returns anything?
residue.special_surfaces: Any endpoints not observable with a plain HTTP client? (websocket, gRPC stream, webhook receiver, queue consumer)

row.value: return value / thrown error / mutated state
row.terminal_action: the call that performs the operation
row.receipt: a unit test against the public API

residue.access: How does a consumer obtain the built package to verify against? (local pack, private registry, path or workspace dependency)
residue.shortcut: Any way to exercise the public API without publishing? (examples dir, workspace link, playground)
residue.fixtures: Is there a sample consumer or fixture project the package must work inside?
residue.special_surfaces: Any behavior that only shows in a consumer's environment? (type-only exports, bundler plugin, peer-dependency interplay)

row.terminal_action: the subcommand that performs the effect
row.receipt: run-and-assert: a unit test, or receipt-cmd: the invocation itself (mytool ... expect:/<expected stdout>/)

residue.access: How is the tool installed and invoked where it is verified? (npx, built binary, container) and which credentials or env vars does a run need?
residue.shortcut: Any flag or env var that makes a run reproducible or unattended? (--yes, fixed seed, sandbox or dry-run mode)
residue.fixtures: Is there a fixture project or input set the command must run against, or does any directory do?
residue.special_surfaces: Any behavior that only shows with a terminal attached? (interactive prompts, TTY-only output, colors, progress bars)

residue.access: How does an agent reach a signed-in state on the test build? (test account, simulator or device, dev bypass)
residue.shortcut: Any dev-mode shortcut? (debug menu, fixed OTP, mock backend)
residue.fixtures: Does the test backend carry realistic data, or must it be seeded first?
residue.special_surfaces: Any screens that need a real device rather than a simulator? (camera, push, biometrics, payments)

residue.access: How is the packaged app installed and launched where it is verified, and does it need an account?
residue.shortcut: Any dev-mode shortcut? (dev flag, mock services, seeded profile)
residue.fixtures: Is there a fixture profile or workspace the app must open, or does a clean install do?
residue.special_surfaces: Any behavior that needs the real OS rather than automation? (native dialogs, file associations, tray)

row.value: row counts, column values, aggregates, schema
row.terminal_action: the job run that writes the output
row.receipt: a data test (dbt test, Great Expectations), or receipt-cmd: an assertion query (select count(*) ... where <invariant violated> expect:/^0$/)

residue.access: How does an agent read the destination store where outputs land? (connection or proxy, read-only role, which environment)
residue.shortcut: Any way to run the job against a small or sandboxed slice? (env flag, sample partition, dry-run)
residue.fixtures: Is there a known-good baseline or seed dataset to reconcile against, or is the source the only truth?
residue.special_surfaces: Any outputs only observable downstream? (dashboards, exported files, a consuming service)

row.surface: the prediction/metric on a pinned eval
row.value: a metric (accuracy/F1/loss) on a fixed eval set, or a specific prediction
row.build_artifact: the model artifact version + serving deploy
row.receipt: an eval test on a pinned dataset (regression = red)

residue.access: How does an agent run the eval and read its metrics? (eval command, pinned dataset location, credentials)
residue.shortcut: Any smaller pinned eval that runs fast?
residue.fixtures: Where is the pinned eval set and the baseline metric it must not regress?
residue.special_surfaces: Any behavior only observable in serving? (latency, live traffic, A/B)

row.value: the resource attribute (a rule, a replica count)
row.receipt: a plan/policy test (conftest/OPA), or receipt-cmd: the plan-diff itself (terraform plan -detailed-exitcode; exit 0 = converged)

residue.access: Where can an agent plan and read back resource state safely? (sandbox account or workspace, read-only role, state backend)
residue.shortcut: Any way to converge a small scope? (target or workspace flag, local cluster, plan-only)
residue.fixtures: Is there a reference environment whose state is the baseline to compare against?
residue.special_surfaces: Any resources only observable from inside the network or via a console? (private endpoints, IAM effects, DNS propagation)

row.value: column type/existence, row values incl. legacy rows
row.build_artifact: the migrated DB at the deployed sha
row.receipt: a migration test on a fixture, or receipt-cmd: a query asserting the migrated schema/rows (incl. legacy) via expect:/.../

residue.access: How does an agent query the migrated database where it is verified? (connection or proxy, read-only role, which environment)
residue.shortcut: Any way to run the migration on a copy or fixture first? (snapshot restore, sandbox DB)
residue.fixtures: Is there a legacy-row fixture that must survive the migration, or a source of truth to reconcile against by value?
residue.special_surfaces: Any effects only observable through the application rather than SQL? (serializer output, cached views)

residue.access: Which network or fork does an agent deploy and call against, with which funded account?
residue.shortcut: Any local chain or fork that reproduces mainnet state?
residue.fixtures: Is there a pinned block or state fixture the tests run against?
residue.special_surfaces: Any behavior only observable on-chain over time? (block timing, oracle inputs)

row.surface: the injected UI / the modified page
row.observe_by: a browser with the extension loaded
row.receipt: an e2e with the extension loaded

residue.access: How is the extension loaded into a browser where it is verified, and does the target site need a signed-in state?
residue.shortcut: Any dev shortcut? (unpacked load, mock page, test host)
residue.fixtures: Is there a fixture page the extension must act on?
residue.special_surfaces: Any behavior only observable in the real store build? (permission prompts, MV3 service-worker lifecycle)

residue.access: How does an agent flash and observe the target? (device or emulator, serial or debug interface, credentials)
residue.shortcut: Any emulator or HIL rig that stands in for hardware?
residue.fixtures: Which signals or registers are the baseline to assert against?
residue.special_surfaces: Any behavior only observable on real hardware? (timing, power, peripherals)

row.observe_by: a state-reading harness or a deterministic sim

residue.access: How does an agent launch a build and read game state? (state-reading harness, deterministic sim, save file)
residue.shortcut: Any deterministic seed or headless mode?
residue.fixtures: Is there a pinned scenario or save that reproduces the reported state?
residue.special_surfaces: Any behavior only observable rendered or with input devices? (frame timing, controller)

row.surface: the recipient's inbox/device + the rendered message
row.value: the recipient-facing content: the embedded URL's host and that it resolves (2xx, right page), the token/attachment works; NOT the provider's accepted/sent count
row.observe_by: opening the delivered message as the recipient
row.terminal_action: the recipient acting on it (the link opens and works)
row.build_artifact: the SENDING environment's config (base URL, from-address, signing keys) at your sha; jobs/workers do not inherit the app's env
row.receipt: a canary send to a controlled address, opened end to end, or receipt-cmd: capturing the emitted URL and asserting expect:/^https:\/\/<prod-host>\// plus a curl -fsS that it resolves

residue.access: Where does a canary send land that an agent can open? (controlled inbox or device, capture endpoint)
residue.shortcut: Any capture mode that intercepts sends without delivering? (sandbox provider, log-only flag)
residue.fixtures: Is there a fixture recipient and a known-good message to compare against?
residue.special_surfaces: Any part only observable in the recipient's client? (rendering, link tracking, attachments)

residue.access: How does an agent reach the place where the behavior is observable, and what access does that need?
residue.shortcut: Any shortcut that makes it reachable or reproducible without production access?
residue.fixtures: Does the verify environment hold realistic data or inputs, or must something be seeded first?
residue.special_surfaces: Any behavior not observable through the primary tool named in observe-by? (comma-separated)
